note: Mostly correct but one part is overstated. PlantWild (ACM MM 2024, peer-reviewed; arXiv 2408.03120): 18,542 images, 89 classes (56 diseased, 33 healthy), release promised in future tense via tqwei05.github.io/PlantWild. All confirmed. PP2021 (FGVC8 page): grew from 3,651 to more than 23,000 images, two disease categories added, multi-disease-per-leaf objective. Confirmed. Overstatement: in PP2020 (arXiv 2004.11958, preprint, used for the CVPR 2020 FGVC7 Kaggle challenge), the 3,651 images were manually captured, but only a pilot subset was expert-annotated for scab, cedar apple rust, and healthy. Not all 3,651 are 'expert-annotated'. The ~97% CNN accuracy on a held-out test set is confirmed.

TinyCNN (arXiv 2609.20290, preprint, Ho-Lam & Nguyen) abstract has the quoted Grad-CAM phrase about off-leaf, background-driven attention and shortcut learning, under PlantVillage-to-PlantDoc evaluation. It reports no calibration metrics, only accuracy, macro-F1 and Wilson CIs. AgriPath (arXiv 2603.13354v3, preprint) reports no ECE or other calibration metric, only macro-F1/P/R and PSR. Section 4.6 has the qualitative cases: CNN ~66% on leaf spot for a corn common rust image (~28% on the correct class), and CLIP at 45% late blight vs 42% early blight. 'Rarely measure calibration' is an absence claim and best-effort: a quick search found a grape-field study that does report ECE, which fits 'rarely' rather than 'never'.

Guo et al., ICML 2017 (peer-reviewed). Abstract: modern networks 'are poorly calibrated'. Temperature scaling, a single-parameter variant of Platt scaling, is 'surprisingly effective' on most datasets. Fitting on a held-out validation set is standard in the paper body; the abstract doesn't state it. In-distribution framing is fair.

Ovadia et al., NeurIPS 2019 (peer-reviewed). Abstract quotes match exactly. The abstract says 'methods that marginalize over models' rather than 'ensembles', but the paper body finds deep ensembles perform best across most metrics under shift. Claim is consistent.

Geifman & El-Yaniv, 'Selective Classification for Deep Neural Networks', NeurIPS 2017 (peer-reviewed; the arXiv page lists no venue). Abstract: 2% top-5 ImageNet error guaranteed with probability 99.9% at almost 60% test coverage. Numbers match. The risk-coverage framing is from the paper body, not the abstract.
